ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r1.claim: Quraysh’s knowledge of Makkah’s history should prevent them from mistaking current affluence for immunity; God can destroy them, especially while they neglect Abraham’s purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r1.anchor: there is no reason for those who know the early history of this area to be misled by their current affluence

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r5.claim: Al-Harith ibn ʿAmir ibn Nawfal complained that following Muhammad had cost him much money through expiations and liabilities prescribed after sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r5.anchor: وقيل: الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل، وكان إذا أذنب استفتى النبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r6.claim: Readers vary the vowels and doubling in lubadan: most use a damma then fatḥa, Abu Jaʿfar doubles bāʾ, he and Zayd ibn ʿAli also have a still bāʾ, and Mujahid and Ibn Abi al-Zinad use two dammas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لبدا، بضم اللام وفتح الباء وأبو جعفر: بشد الباء

MAJAZ:v2p299/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p299/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p299/r2.claim: Libadan means piled-up wealth, from the verb talabbada.
MAJAZ:v2p299/r2.anchor: «مالا لبدا» (6) فعل من التلبد وهو المال الكثير بعضه على بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p430/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p430/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p430/r11.claim: He boasts of spending abundant, piled-up wealth against Muhammad; Abu Jaafar doubles the b in لبدا as a plural, while others read it lightly as a plural of a heap or as a singular form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p430/r11.anchor: {يقول أهلكت} يعني أنفقت، {مالا لبدا} أي كثيرا بعضه على بعض، من التلبيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r4.claim: Boasting that he spent much wealth suggests the speaker still possesses far more, revealing pride in indebtedness over all people and desire for immeasurable riches.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r4.anchor: فعلم أن مراد الإشارة إلى أن معه أضعاف ما أنفق من حيث إنه حقره بلفظ الإهلاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r5.claim: The two desires are illustrated by a report that Adam’s child would keep wanting gold and by the statement that nothing fills his belly but earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r5.anchor: حديث ( لو أن لابن آدم واد من ذهب )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar’s geminated reading of lubad treats it as a plural like rukkaʿ, emphasizing wealth stacked beyond counting or the capacity of the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r6.anchor: جاءت قراءة أبي جعفر بالتشديد على أنه جمع لا بد كركع وراكع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p428/r7.claim: The boast presents wealth as a means to impose favors, enslave free people, and command a large following and unquestioned obedience.

NAHHAS:v5p229/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r3.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p229/r3.claim: One view says the boast about spending heaps of wealth was meant to deter good deeds; another says it was spoken in regret, as the following reply suggests.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r3.anchor: قيل يدافع بهذا عن فعل الخيرات وقيل قال هذا تندما ويدل على هذا الجواب ما بعده

NAHHAS:v5p229/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p229/r4.claim: Lubadan can be a plural of lubb or a singular collective like ḥuṭam; Abū Jaʿfar's reported reading is a plural of lābid, and Mujāhid reads lubud, a plural of lubūd. All mean many.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r4.anchor: ولا نعلم اختلافا في معناه أنه الكثير

DURR-FULL:v8p519/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r4.claim: He identified the father and offspring as Adam and his children; human life is toil in worldly and afterlife affairs, and labad means much.
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.claim: He identified the father as Adam, offspring as his children, hardship as severity, labad as much, and ‘does he think no one sees’ as no one can overpower him.
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r3.claim: Mujahid says the boast of spending heaps means spending much.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r3.anchor: يقول اهلكت مالا لبدا قال : كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.claim: The next lines expose the boast of wasteful spending as a false virtue among pre-Islamic Arabs; the cited ʿAntara poem boasts of spending wealth while preserving honor, and the statement is a circumstantial description of the human's hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.anchor: أعقبت مساوي نفسه بمذام أقواله ، وهو التفخر الكاذب والتمدح بإتلاف المال في غير صلاح .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is a rebuking question with its interrogative particle omitted: the boaster wasted wealth on gambling and wine, so why did he not spend generously on liberation and feeding during famine?
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.anchor: وتكون ( لا اقتحم العقبة ) استفهاما حذف منه أداته . وهو استفهام إنكار ، والمعنى : أنه يدعي إهلاك مال كثير

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r3.claim: He reads lubadan with a doubled bāʾ as a plural, like rākiʿ and rukkaʿ.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وحده: لبدا مشددة الباء على الجمع

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r4.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r4.claim: He reads lubadan with ḍamma on both lām and bāʾ, like amrun nukur or rijāl junub.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r4.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد بضم اللام والباء، كقولك: أمر نكر، ورجال جنب

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r5.claim: The common form, with ḍamma on lām and fatḥ on bāʾ, may be a plural of lubda or a singular form like qaym.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r5.anchor: والقراء كلهم على ضم اللام وفتح الباء مخففة، وفيه وجهان

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r9.claim: Labd means much or piled up, from tَلَبُّد, layering things together; Arabs say a poor person has neither support nor wealth piled up.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r9.anchor: واللبد: الكثير، وهو مأخوذ من: تلبد الشيء، إذا تراكب بعضه على بعض

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r3.claim: Another report identifies al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who said he had spent a large pile of money opposing Muḥammad.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r3.anchor: وقيل: نزلت الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة، كان يقول: أهلكت مالا لبدا

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r4.claim: A further report identifies al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal, who complained that atonements and expenses since becoming Muslim had consumed his wealth.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r4.anchor: وقيل: بل نزلت في الحارث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r5.claim: The verses apply generally; the wording is the basis for interpretation rather than the specific occasion.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r5.anchor: والأولى أنها على عمومها، فالمعتبر باللفظ، لا بالسبب

ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r7.claim: Labad means much, packed or stuck together; labad is also read as the plural of lābid.
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r7.anchor: كثير بعضه قد لبد ببعض، وفعل للكثرة،

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.claim: The biblical allusion overwrites the heroic worldview carried by the poetry cited in verse 6, making scripture an ally against the values of canonical pre-Islamic verse.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die durch die Anspielung in V. 90:6 repräsentierte Dichtung und das von ihr transportierte heroische Weltbild werden durch eine – vielleicht aus gottesdienstlichen Lesungen vertraute – Bibel-Referenz überschrieben

TABATABAI:90:4-10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:4-10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:90:4-10/r4.claim: The context suggests a person who professed or approached Islam had spent money and boasted of wasting a great deal; God answers that salvation requires the difficult charity and joining the believers.
TABATABAI:90:4-10/r4.anchor: مشعر بأنه كان هناك بعض من أظهر الإسلام أو مال إليه فقد أنفق بعض ماله وامتن به

TABRISI:90:1-20#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#3/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20#3/r15.claim: The man boasts that he spent abundant wealth opposing the Prophet.
TABRISI:90:1-20#3/r15.anchor: هذا الإنسان فقال { يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا

TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r1.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r1.claim: The boastful person was al-Harith ibn ʿAmir ibn Nawfal, who complained that expiation and spending after converting to Muhammad's religion had consumed his wealth.
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r1.anchor: هو الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف وذلك أنه أذنب ذنبا فاستفتى رسول الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p258/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p258/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p258/r4.claim: People commonly act with arrogance and oppression, relying on their might and ignoring their Creator; remembering God's power would humble them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p258/r4.anchor: يتصورون أنه لا يَتمكَّنُ منهم أحدٌ ولا يقدر عليهم أحد، ولذا تراهم يعيشون في غطرسة وكبرياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.claim: Labad contributes to the surah's collective pattern: parents and offspring, paired faculties and paths, several ascent duties, believers advising one another, and disbelievers gathered in Hell; the plain word many would lose this effect.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.anchor: وفي ذكر المؤمنين بصيغة الجمع {الذين آمَنُواْ} ، واجتماعهم على التواصي بالصبر والمرحمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.claim: The man who boasts of wasting much money spent it in the wrong place, since he neither fed a hungry person nor freed anyone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.anchor: فقد أهلكها هذا القائل في غير محلها، فلم يطعمْ جائعاً ولم يفكَّ رقبة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.claim: The boastful spender needs mercy so he directs his wealth to the needy instead of wasting it uselessly; the enslaved person also needs compassion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.anchor: وهذا الذي أهلك مالاً لُبداً، يحتاج إلى الرحمة لينفق المال على ذوي الحاجة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r4.claim: Other expressions preserve breadth: the questioned person may be anyone or a particular person, and his claim to have spent much may describe display, opposition to the Prophet, another purpose, or a lie.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r4.anchor: و {أَيَحْسَبُ} تحتمل العموم والخصوص، فهي تحتمل كل إنسان، وتحتمل إنساناً معيناً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r5.claim: Labad can be a plural meaning heaps or a singular adjective meaning piled up or obstinate.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p283/r5.anchor: و"اللَّبد" تحتمل الجمع وتحتمل المفرد، فعلى الجمع تكون جمع (لُبدة)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.claim: The surah is woven around five threads: human toil, breadth of meaning, collective action, patience, and mercy.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.anchor: خط المكابدة التي تدل عليه الآية {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان فِي كَبَدٍ}

THALABI:v10p207/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p207/r20.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي الضحى
THALABI:v10p207/r20.claim: The speaker boasts of spending a piled-up amount of wealth, partly in opposition to Muhammad.
THALABI:v10p207/r20.anchor: أخبرني أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس. يقول أهلكت أنفقت مالا لبدا بعضه على بعض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r1.claim: The man falsely boasts that he spent much wealth in opposition to Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r1.anchor: { يقول أهلكت مالا } على عداوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { لبدا } كثيرا بعضه على بعض

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r2.claim: Someone who spent heaps of wealth should have directed some of it to orphans, the poor, and debtors instead of wasting it unjustly.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r2.anchor: كان ينبغي له أن يُنفق على هؤلاء المساكين واليتامى والغارمين شيئاً من ماله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p408/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p408/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p408/r1.claim: Al-Humazah's hoarder thinks wealth makes him immortal; shutting him into Hell's sealed columns fittingly mirrors his hoarding, unlike al-Balad's description of someone who squandered wealth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p408/r1.anchor: فكما حفظ الكافر المال وجمعه وحسب أنه يخلده

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r8.claim: The boast about heaps of wealth was made to flaunt superiority before believers; calling the spending waste signals that it brought no genuine benefit, unlike feeding the poor.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r8.anchor: Bunu mü’minlere karşı azamet satmak üzere gurur ve iftihar ile söylüyor ve gösteriş için sarfettiği malları kasdediyor

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r9.claim: Another interpretation says the wealth was spent in hostility toward the Messenger, to display the intensity of enmity.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r9.anchor: Resûlullah’a adâvetinin şiddetini izhar için ona düşmanlık yolunda sarfettiği malları kasdettiği de söylenmiştir

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r10.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r10.claim: Al-Harith ibn Nawfal reportedly complained that since obeying Muhammad he had spent much on expiations and liabilities; this was resentment toward religion and refusal to obey the Prophet.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r10.anchor: Mukātil’den mervîdir ki: Hâris b. Nevfel bir günah işlediği zaman Resûlullah’tan istiftâ ederdi

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r11.speaker: some exegetes
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r11.claim: Some read “he says” as future: the boast will be made at the Resurrection when the speaker discovers that his spending did not benefit him.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r11.anchor: يَقُولُ hâl değil, istikbal içindir. Bunu kıyamet günü söyleyecek demektir

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r12.claim: Lubad means a great quantity piled layer upon layer, like felt.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r12.anchor: “Lübed” “sured” vezninde çok mal mânasınadır ki, sanki birbiri üstüne yığıla yığıla keçe

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.claim: God’s gifts guide humanity toward its purpose and establish divine knowledge and power to reckon and punish; the contrast between tranquil and unbelieving souls further explains hardship.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.anchor: halkettiği insana ve bu meyanda bilhassa kuvvet ve malıyla iftihar eden

BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r3.claim: The boastful speaker says he spent great heaps of wealth for reputation; pre-Islamic Arabs called such ostentation generosity and honor, though the word squandered shows it is truly wasted.
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r3.anchor: أنفقت كقول العرب خسرت عليه كذا إذا أنفق عليه

BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r4.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r4.claim: Aisha asked whether Abdullah ibn Judan's pre-Islamic charity and care for kin would benefit him; the Prophet answered that it would not, since he never sought forgiveness for Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r4.anchor: ما قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها في حق عبد الله ابن جدعان كان في الجاهلية

BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r5.claim: The Prophet said the charitable deeds would not benefit Abdullah ibn Judan because he never prayed for forgiveness on Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r5.anchor: لا ينفعه لأنه لم يقل يوما رب اغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين

BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r6.claim: A person will not move on Judgment Day until questioned about his lifespan, wealth's source and spending, deeds, and love for the Prophet's family.
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث لا تزول قدما العبد يوم القيامة حتى يسأل عن أربع عن عمره

QASHANI:90:5-7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:5-7/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:5-7/r1.claim: Thick veiling by nature and sickness of heart makes the person think no one can overpower him; he boasts of having spent much on public favors as a way to lord it over people, mistaking wasteful display for virtue.
QASHANI:90:5-7/r1.anchor: لغلظ حجابه ومرض قلبه لاحتجابه بالطبيعة

QASHANI:90:5-7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:5-7/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:5-7/r2.claim: The Arabic boast about having expended much can mean spending on someone to claim superiority, with Arab usage cited for the expression.
QASHANI:90:5-7/r2.anchor: إذا أنفق عليه يتفضل على الناس بالتبذير والإسراف

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says the man spent heaps of money obstructing God's path, and the one he thinks did not see him is God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : اهلكت مالا لبدا قال : انفقت مالا في الصد عن سبيل الله ايحسب ان لم يره أحد قال : الاحد : الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj presents the boast as a claim of abundant wealth and favor, then answers it by recalling the gifts of eyes and other blessings.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله : يقول اهلكت مالا لبدا قال : ايمن علينا فما فضلناه افضل الم نجعل له عينين وكذا وكذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r4.claim: The majority read lubadan with a short u and open bāʾ as the plural of a clump of wool or hair matted together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r4.anchor: و { لبدا } بضم اللام وفتح الموحدة في قراءة الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads lubaddan with a geminated bāʾ, parsing it either as a plural of lābid, 'gathered together,' or as a noun on the faʿal pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r5.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر { لبدا } بضم اللام وتشديد الباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r10.speaker: الجمهور ومجاهد وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r10.claim: Readers vary in the vowels and consonant doubling of labadan, but each reading means abundant, densely piled wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r10.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله «لبدا» ، فقرأ جمهور القراء بضم اللام وفتح الباء،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r1.claim: Labad means a great deal of wealth piled together; Abū ʿUbayda derives it from piling, Ibn Qutayba describes piled wealth, and al-Zajjāj treats it as an intensive expression of abundance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r1.anchor: أي كثيرا قال أبو عبيدة هو فعل من التلبد وهو المال الكثير بعضه على بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وعائشة وأبو عبد الرحمن وقتادة وأبو العالية وأبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r2.claim: These readers pronounce labadan with ḍamma on lām and geminated, open bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وعائشة وأبو عبد الرحمن وقتادة وأبو العالية وأبو جعفر لبدا بضم اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبو المتوكل وأبو عمران
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r3.claim: These readers pronounce labdan with fatḥa on lām and a light, quiescent bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وأبو المتوكل وأبو عمران لبدا بفتح اللام وتسكين الباء خفيفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r4.speaker: عثمان بن عفان والحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r4.claim: These readers pronounce lubudan with ḍamma on both lām and bāʾ and no gemination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ عثمان بن عفان والحسن ومجاهد لبدا برفع اللام والباء وتخفيفهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r5.speaker: علي وابن أبي الجوزاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r5.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn Abī al-Jawzāʾ pronounce libadan with kasra on lām and fatḥa on bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي وابن أبي الجوزاء لبدا بكسر اللام وفتح الباء مخففة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r6.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r6.claim: One account says he boasted of spending much wealth against Muḥammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما أنه أراد أهلكت مالا كثيرا في عداوة محمد قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r7.claim: Another says he regretted having spent so much in God's cause and on expiations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p130#2/r7.anchor: والثاني أنفقت في سبيل الله وفي الكفارات مالا كثيرا قاله مقاتل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r4.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r4.claim: They say the person's boast means that he spent a great amount of wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r4.anchor: أي: يقول ابن آدم: أنفقت مالا لبدا، أي: كثيرا. قاله مجاهد [والحسن] (2) وقتادة، والسدي، وغيرهم.

FARRA:v3p263/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p263/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p263/r1.claim: Labad means abundant; some call its singular labda and its collective plural labad, while others treat labad as a singular on patterns such as quṯam and ḥuṭam.
FARRA:v3p263/r1.anchor: اللبد: الكثير. قال بعضهم واحدته: لبدة، ولبد جماع. وجعله بعضهم على جهة: قثم، وحطم واحدا،

FARRA:v3p263/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p263/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر المدني
FARRA:v3p263/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī reads labadan with gemination, as though saying wealth that never ends; money and wealth can mean the same thing.
FARRA:v3p263/r2.anchor: الكثير. وقرأ أبو جعفر المدني. «مالا لبدا» مشددة مثل ركع، فكأنه أراد:

FARRA:v3p263/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p263/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p263/r11.claim: He claimed he had spent much wealth opposing Muhammad, but this was a lie; God saw what he spent.
FARRA:v3p263/r11.anchor:
والله قادر عليه.
ثم قال: يقول:
أنفقت مالا كثيرا في عداوة محمد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#4/r1.claim: Labad means abundant, from piling and sticking things on top of one another.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#4/r1.anchor: {مالا لبدا} أي كثيرا. وهو من "التلبد": كأن بعضه على بعض.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.claim: The person questioned is a Quraysh notable who assumes there will be no Resurrection or retribution despite his strength and mistreatment of believers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.anchor: أيظن هذا الصنديد القوي في قومه المتضعف للمؤمنين : أن لن تقوم قيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r4.claim: His boast of heaps of spending refers to ostentatious expenditures pre-Islamic Arabs called virtues, high-minded acts, and boasts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r4.anchor: يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها مكارم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r9.claim: Lubadan is read with damma or kasra for heaps; another reading treats it as a plural of piled-up things, with labadan as a plural of labid.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r9.anchor: ( لبدا ) قرىء بالضم والكسر : جمع لبدة ولبدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r4.claim: Beneficial spending pleases God, unlike ostentatious heaps of wealth, which resemble a crop struck by a fierce wind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r4.anchor: لا أن يهلك مالا لبدا في الرياء والفخار

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r10.claim: Labadan may mean a large amount of money.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r10.anchor: لبدا } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : يعني كثيرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r11.claim: Labadan may mean piled together, like felt, because the wealth is packed one layer on another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r11.anchor: مجتمعا بعضه على بعض , ومنه سمي اللبد لاجتماعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r12.claim: A third possibility is old wealth, deriving the word from abad or from the proverbically ancient Lubad, emphasizing how long it was hoarded.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r12.anchor: لاشتقاقه من الأبد , أو للمبالغة في قدمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r13.claim: The speaker may be Abu al-Ashadd al-Jumahi, who spent much wealth opposing the Messenger and God's path, or al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r14.claim: His statement may boast of extravagant spending and thus show insolence, or lament the loss and show regret.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r14.anchor: فيكون طغيانا منه . الثاني : أن يكون أسفا عليه

MUJAHID:v2p759#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p759#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p759#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says libadan means a great deal of wealth.
MUJAHID:v2p759#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ مالا لبدا ﴾ قال مالا كثيرا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#4/r1.claim: Lubad means much, from a mass or heap; the boast concerns abundant spending on what pre-Islamic Arabs called noble deeds and honors.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#4/r1.anchor: أى كثيرا جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد أى كثروا جتمع يريد كثرة ما أنفقه

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r2.claim: Ahlaktu means “I spent”; libada means abundant, accumulated wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r2.anchor: { يقول أهلكت } أي أنفقت. { مالا لبدا } أي كثيرا مجتمعا

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a servant claims he spent and paid zakat, but is told he did so only to be called generous; he is sent to Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r4.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة قال: يوقف العبد، فيقال ماذا عملت في المال الذي رزقتك؟ فيقول: أنفقته وزكيته

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r5.claim: Qatada says a person will be asked where his money came from and how he spent it.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r5.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة: إنك مسؤول عن مالك من أين جمعت؟ وكيف أنفقت؟

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu al-Ashaddayn falsely boasted that he spent much wealth opposing Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: كان أبو الأشدين يقول: أنفقت في عداوة محمد مالا كثيرا وهو في ذلك كاذب

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r7.claim: Muqatil says the passage was revealed about al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal, who claimed expiations and expenses exhausted his wealth since entering Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في الحارث بن عامر بن نوفل، أذنب فاستفتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says al-Harith’s complaint may be arrogant boasting about expenditure or regret at the expense.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r8.anchor: وهذا القول منه يحتمل أن يكون استطالة بما أنفق، فيكون طغيانا منه، أو أسفا عليه، فيكون ندما منه

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r9.claim: Abu Jaafar reads labada with a doubled, open bāʾ as a plural like rakiʿ/rukaʿ.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر «مالا لبدا» بتشديد الباء مفتوحة

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r10.speaker: مجاهد، حميد
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r10.claim: Mujahid and Humayd read labud with bāʾ and lām rounded, a plural of labud.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد بضم الباء واللام مخففا، جمع لبود

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r11.claim: The remaining readers use variants of labda/lubda, meaning a felted mass and thus abundance.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r11.anchor: الباقون بضم اللام وكسرها وفتح الباء مخففا، جمع لبدة ولبدة، وهو ما تلبد يريد الكثرة

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet read yahsabu with a rounded sīn at both occurrences.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r12.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقرأ «أيحسب» بضم السين في الموضعين

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r13.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r13.claim: Al-Hasan paraphrases the boast as: I squandered much money, so who will audit me? Let me count it myself.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: يقول أتلفت مالا كثيرا، فمن يحاسبني به دعني أحسبه

QUTB-ZILAL:90:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:6/r1.claim: When called to give for good, a person boasts that he has already spent a great deal and treats past spending as sufficient.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:6/r1.anchor: وأنفقت شيئا كثيرا فحسبي ماأنفقت وما بذلت

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats lubad as an intensive form for wealth piled up in great quantity.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : لبد ، فعل من التلبيد وهو المال الكثير بعضه على بعض

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says lubad is an intensive form for abundance, like ḥuṭam describing someone who breaks much.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : فعل للكثرة يقال رجل حطم إذا كان كثير الحطم

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives labda as singular and lubad as plural, while others treat lubad as singular; either way it means much.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : واحدته لبدة ولبد جمع وجعله بعضهم واحدا

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r4.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r4.claim: Al-Layth says wealth called lubad is so plentiful that its owner does not fear it will run out.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r4.anchor: قال الليث : مال لبد لا يخاف فناؤه من كثرته

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r5.claim: Razi links the word's explanation to the same form in 72:19.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكرنا تفسير هذا الحرف عند قوله : { يكونون عليه لبدا

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r6.claim: The unbeliever boasts of spending abundant wealth in hostility to Muhammad on what pre-Islamic Arabs called noble deeds and pride.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#2/r6.anchor: والمعنى أن هذا الكافر يقول : أهلكت في عداوة محمد مالا كثيرا

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r6.claim: Hasan says the boaster asks who will account for the wealth he claims to have spent; the answer is the One who created his limbs.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن : قال : { أهلكت مالا لبدا }

STUDYQURAN:90:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:5/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:5/r1.claim: The question concerns whether man expects accountability for all his acts; wealth-deluded people forget God controls provision and can remove it at any time, and answer for how they obtain and spend it regardless of philanthropy.
STUDYQURAN:90:5/r1.anchor: V. 5 asks, “Does man not think that he will be held accountable for all his actions?”

STUDYQURAN:90:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:5/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:90:5/r2.claim: Some identify the speaker as Ḥarith ibn ʿĀmir, who complained he had spent his wealth on expiations and payments since entering Muhammad's religion.
STUDYQURAN:90:5/r2.anchor: Some have said that v. 6 refers to Ḥarith ibn ʿĀmir

SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r1.claim: Yaqūlu may be an independent clause or a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مستأنفة، وأن تكون حالا.

SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r2.claim: The common reading has lubadan with ḍamma on lām and fatḥa on bāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar doubles bāʾ and is also reported with it unvowelled, while Mujāhid and Ibn Abī al-Zinād use two ḍammas.
SAMIN-DURR:90:6/r2.anchor: بضم اللام وفتح الباء. وشدد أبو جعفر الباء، وعنه أيضا سكونها.

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r1.claim: The strong man falsely claims he spent much wealth in hostility toward Muḥammad; libadan describes wealth piled up.
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r1.anchor: أهلكت مالا كثيرا، في عداوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأنفقت ذلك فيه، وهو كاذب في قوله ذلك

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses libadan as abundant wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {مالا لبدا} [البلد: 6] يعني باللبد: المال الكثير

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the wealth was abundant.

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r4.claim: Qatāda likewise glosses the wealth as much or abundant.
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أهلكت مالا لبدا} [البلد: 6] : أي: كثيرا

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says libad means abundant.
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {مالا لبدا} [البلد: 6] قال: اللبد: الكثير

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r6.speaker: عامة قراء الأمصار
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r6.claim: Most regional readers use a light bāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar alone is reported with a doubled bāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r6.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء الأمصار: {مالا لبدا} [البلد: 6] بتخفيف الباء. وقرأه أبو جعفر بتشديدها

TAB-FULL:v24p413/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p413/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the light reading because the authoritative readers agree on it.

TABATABAI:90:18-20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:18-20/r8.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:90:18-20/r8.claim: Al-Qummī glosses lubad as accumulated or gathered wealth.
TABATABAI:90:18-20/r8.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي { يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا } قال اللبد المجتمع

TABATABAI:90:18-20/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:18-20/r9.speaker: مقاتل
TABATABAI:90:18-20/r9.claim: Muqātil says the verse concerns al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, who complained that expiations and spending since entering Islam had consumed his wealth.
TABATABAI:90:18-20/r9.anchor: وفي المجمع في الآية قيل هو الحارث بن نوفل بن عبد مناف

ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n4/r1.claim: The boast implies inexhaustible resources and possibilities; as “man” means humanity, it represents the decadence-era belief that human ambition has no limits and worldly interests alone define right and wrong.
ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n4/r1.anchor: his resources - and, therefore, his possibilities - are inexhaustible

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r1.claim: “Lubadan” is a form of piling and means much wealth stacked together.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: لبدا: فعل من التلبد، وهو المال الكثير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r2.claim: The form intensifies abundance, like calling a man “crusher” because he crushes much.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وفعل للكثرة، يقال: رجل حطم إذا كان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r3.claim: “Lubad” may be collective, with “lubda” as its singular, or an intensive singular; either way it means a great deal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p19#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: واحدته لبدة، ولبد جماع،

WAHIDI-QT:90:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:6/r1.claim: He claims to have spent a great, piled-up sum opposing Muhammad, but he lies.
WAHIDI-QT:90:6/r1.anchor: { يقول أهلكت مالا } على عداوة محمد ص { لبدا } كثيرا بعضه على بعض وهو كاذب في ذلك

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: Lubad means piled up or abundant; the verse alludes to wasteful spending, a virtue in the pre-Islamic poetic hero ideal.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu lubad, „übereinandergeschichtet, massenhaft“, s. WKAS, s. v. l-b-d, Nr. 2. Der Vers spielt auf die in der altarabischen Dichtung als Tugend gewertete Verschwendungssucht des Dichter-Helden an

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r2.claim: Taʾabbaṭa Šarran's poem rebukes someone for wasting wealth instead of saving it; ʿAntara positively boasts of drinking until his wealth is ruined.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r2.anchor: ʾahlakta mālan lau qaniʿta bihī, „Du hast deinen Besitz vertan, hättest du ihn doch zurückbehalten!“ sowie, positiv gewendet, den folgenden Vers des ʿAntara

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r3.claim: This ostentatious waste contrasts with 104:2–3, which condemns uncontrolled accumulation as security or immortality, likely reflecting urban merchant mentality.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:6:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Im Gegensatz zu der hier angeprangerten ostentativen Verschwendung von Besitz

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza resumes the human-being statement at the introduction’s end and consists of two triplets marked by rhyme; the repeated third-person polemical questions formally unify them.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz, das pronominal an den ʾinsān-Spruch am Ende des Einleitungsgesätzes anknüpft, gliedert sich in zwei reimlich voneinander abgesetzte Dreiergruppen

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.claim: The first triplet attacks possessiveness and imagined self-sufficiency apart from God, a stance called istaġnā in other early suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die erste Gesätzhälfte ist eine an 104 erinnernde Besitzpolemik; sie prangert jene menschliche Haltung vermeintlicher Selbstgenügsamkeit und Nicht-Angewiesenheit auf Gott an

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r4.claim: The boast about spending heaps of wealth exemplifies human arrogance by inverting poetry’s positively valued ostentatious generosity; verses 13–16 show the positive use of wealth.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r4.anchor: Der Vers invertiert einen ursprünglich positiv konnotierten Topos der altarabischen Dichtung, die dem altarabischen karam-Ideal entsprechende ostentative Verschwendung von Besitz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r2.speaker: Bazı yorumlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r2.claim: One interpretation is that some regretted spending so much money in an effort to make the Prophet fail.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r2.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’i başarısız kılma uğruna harcadıkları onca mala üzülüyorlardı

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r1.claim: Lubad means much accumulated together, from the verb for something clumping together.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r1.anchor: اللبد: هو الكثير المجتمع من تَلَبَّدَ الشيءُ إذا اجتمع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r2.claim: The speaker boasts of spending a great deal of money, or says it regretfully.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية: إنه يقول إنه أنفق مالاً كثيراً، وهو يقول ذاك إما على جهة الافتخار أو على جهة التحسر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r3.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf says he means the large sums spent on pre-Islamic acts called virtues, high deeds, and boasts.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r3.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : "يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها، مكارمَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r4.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r4.claim: One reading takes the utterance as proud ostentation against believers; another places it at Judgment, when the spending proves useless and is called destruction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r4.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "أي: يقول ذلك وقت الاغترار فخراً ومُباهاةً وتَعظُّماً على المؤمنين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r5.claim: Calling spending destruction suits the surah’s hardship and death: the Messenger’s companions suffered, the man imagines none can destroy him, the obstacle may be perilous, the hungry may die, and the left-hand group faces lasting ruin.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p259/r5.anchor: وقد عبر عن الإنفاق بالإهلاك، فإنه لم يقل: (أنفقت مالاً)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r1.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r1.claim: Describing spending as destruction shows disregard: the spender treated his great wealth as wasted rather than expecting benefit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r1.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "وعبر عن الإنفاق بالإهلاك إظهاراً لعدم الاكتراث

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r2.speaker: التبيان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r2.claim: The spendthrift boasts of wasting wealth on desires; had he spent it where God commanded, it would have drawn him near God rather than destroyed it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r2.anchor: وجاء في (التبيان) : "ثم أنكر سبحانه على الإنسان قوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r3.claim: Lubad is more exact than merely saying much because it conveys many things piled together; the Kashshaf notes its variant forms as plurals of lubda.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r3.anchor: واختيار (اللبد) في الآية مكان (الكثير) اختيارٌ دقيق ذلك أن اللبد معناه الكثير المجتمع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r4.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports lubadan with damma or kasra as a plural of lubda or libda, meaning a mass and hence great quantity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r4.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : "لبداً قرىء بالضم والكسر جمع لُبدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r5.claim: The piled wealth echoes the disbelievers massing against the Messenger and Muslims to stop the call, paralleling their joint attempt to destroy his mission.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p260/r5.anchor: فاجتماعُ المال في الإهلاك مناسب لاجتماع الكفرة على الرسول لإهلاكه، وإهلاك دعوته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.speaker: التبيان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.claim: Al-Tibyan notes that lam marks the past, matching the past-tense boast: does the person think nobody saw what he spent and destroyed?
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.anchor: ثم وبخه بقوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ} وأتى ههنا بِلَمْ الدالة على المضي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r3.claim: The tongue and lips enable his boast that he spent a heap, so he uses God’s gifts while opposing God’s allies, messengers, and message.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r3.anchor: وارتباط قوله: {وَلِسَاناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ} بقوله: {يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p265/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p265/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p265/r2.claim: He failed to repay God’s favors with righteous deeds such as freeing people and feeding orphans and the poor; approved giving benefits at God’s sight, unlike wasteful boasting, which is like ruined crops.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p265/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية أنه: "لم يشكر تلك الأيادي والنعم بالأعمال الصالحة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p281/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p281/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p281/r2.claim: The hoarder who gathers and locks away wealth is repaid with sealed Hell doors and columns; al-Balad instead describes someone who squandered wealth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p281/r2.anchor: ذكر في سورة الهمزة أن هذا الكافر يجمع المال ويعدده، ويحفظه فكما حفظ المال وجمعه وأغلق عليه الأبواب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r1.claim: This is the Qur’an’s only use of ‘destroyed’ for money; the word fits the sūra’s hardship, death, obstacle, famine, and wasteful spending, where money spent wrongly is ruined.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r1.anchor: هذه هي الآية الوحيدة في القرآن كله التي استعمل فيها الإهلاك مع المال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r2.claim: Lubad means much gathered together and may be an intensive singular or a plural of lubda; the gathered mass suits the hostile crowds assembled against the Prophet.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r2.anchor: وفيها احتمالان: قد تكون مفرد صيغة مبالغة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r3.claim: The image of gathering recurs across the sūra, and ‘much’ alone would miss this shared sense; the wording serves the sūra’s rhetoric.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p392/r3.anchor: الكثرة لا تنفي الاجتماع لذلك اختيار الإهلاك واللبد متناسب جداً

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads مالا لبدا; Ibn Jinnī allows لبدا as a singular form like زمل, or as a plural of لبد, like قوم from قائم.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: يكون بلفظ الواحد زمل وجباء، ويكون جمع لا بد

QIRAAT-ER:90:6:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:90:6:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:90:6:4#1/r1.claim: The ten-reading form doubles bāʾ, intensifying the sense of compacting or heaping within the same root field.
QIRAAT-ER:90:6:4#1/r1.anchor: with doubled bāʾ; intensifies the compacting or heaping sense

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#4/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses lubadan as abundant wealth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مالا لبدا ﴾ قال مالا كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r1.claim: Lubadan means a great quantity, from the idea of things gathered together; the man says this boastfully to flaunt his spending over believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r1.anchor: يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا أي كثيرا من تلبد الشيء إذا اجتمع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r2.claim: Calling his outlay “wasting” displays his indifference, as though the large amount had been thrown away without concern; one view says he spent it to oppose the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r2.anchor: وعبر عن الأنفاق بالإهلاك إظهارا لعدم الأكتراث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r3.claim: Mujahid? A report from Muqatil says al-Harith ibn Nawfal complained that he had spent great wealth on expiations and penalties since obeying Muhammad, after asking the Prophet how to expiate sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r3.anchor: فعن مقاتل أن الحرث بن نوفل كان إذا أذنب استقتى الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r4.claim: Another view has the speaker make this boast on Judgment Day, when his expenditure proves useless and is therefore called waste.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد ما تقدم أولا إلا أن هذا القول وقت الأنتقام منه وذلك يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r5.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads lubadan with a doubled b; he and Zayd ibn ʿAli also have a form with a still b, while Mujahid and Ibn Abi al-Zinad read both vowels as ḍamma.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر لبدا بشد الباء وعنه وعن زيد بن علي لبدا بسكون الباء

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r1.claim: The boast of having squandered abundant wealth refers to spending for show and rivalry, or in hostility toward the Messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r1.anchor: كثيرا، من تلبد الشيء إذا اجتمع، والمراد ما أنفقه سمعة ومفاخرة

BINTSHATI:v1p180/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r2.claim: He takes the target as humanity generally: people become tyrannical when they think themselves self-sufficient, then deluded by strength and wealth.
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r2.anchor: كما فهم "أبو حيان" وإن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى

BINTSHATI:v1p180/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r3.claim: Lubad occurs only here in the Qur’an and means a dense, accumulated multitude, from wool felted together; the word can describe a lion’s thick mane or dense foliage.
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r3.anchor: لم يأت في القرآن في غير هذا الموضع، وهو في اللغة الكثير المجتمع

BINTSHATI:v1p180/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r4.claim: ‘I destroyed/spent’ rather than ‘I spent’ better suits the speaker’s vanity, arrogance, boasting, and self-display.
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r4.anchor: يقول: أهلكت، ولم يقل: أنفقت، مع قربها، إذ الإهلاك أولى بالغرور والطغيان

BINTSHATI:v1p180/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r5.claim: The indefinite ‘wealth,’ ‘abundant,’ and ‘anyone’ are deliberately unrestricted and general.

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r1.claim: He glosses the boast of spending piled wealth as spending a great deal.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {مالا لبدا} قال: كثيرا

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r2.claim: The speaker spent wealth opposing the path of God.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {أهلكت مالا لبدا} قال: أنفقت مالا في الصد عن سبيل الله

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r4.claim: He reads the boast as a claim of favor, while saying what they preferred was better.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا} قال: أيمن علينا فما فضلناه أفضل

TAB:90:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:90:6/r1.claim: The speaker is a stubborn, self-assured person who claims to have spent much wealth opposing Muhammad; al-Tabari says he is lying.
TAB:90:6/r1.anchor: يقول هذا الجليد الشديد : أهلكت مالاً كثيرا ، في عداوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فأنفقت ذلك فيه ، وهو كاذب في قوله ذلك

TAB:90:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r2.speaker: author
TAB:90:6/r2.claim: Lubad means abundant wealth piled together, from a verb meaning to stick to the ground.
TAB:90:6/r2.anchor: وهو فعل من التلبد ، وهو الكثير ، بعضه على بعض

TAB:90:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:90:6/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses lubad as abundant wealth.
TAB:90:6/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : مالاً لُبَدا يعني باللبد : المال الكثير

TAB:90:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:90:6/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses lubad as much wealth.
TAB:90:6/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد مالاً لُبَدا قال : كثيرا

TAB:90:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB:90:6/r5.claim: Qatada glosses lubad as much wealth.
TAB:90:6/r5.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : أهلكت مالاً لُبَدا : أي كثيرا

TAB:90:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:90:6/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses lubad as abundant wealth.
TAB:90:6/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد ، في قوله : مالاً لُبَدا قال : اللبد : الكثير

TAB:90:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:6/r7.speaker: author
TAB:90:6/r7.claim: Most regional readers lighten the bāʾ, while Abu Jaʿfar geminates it; al-Tabari prefers the light form by reader consensus.
TAB:90:6/r7.anchor: فقرأته عامة قرّاء الأمصار : مالاً لُبَدا بتخفيف الباء . وقرأه أبو جعفر بتشديدها

BURHAN:v2p515/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p515/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p515/r1.claim: On the pattern فعل, لبد means abundant or plentiful, describing the wealth the speaker boasts of spending.
BURHAN:v2p515/r1.anchor: وأما فعل فيكون صفة كقوله تعالى ﴿ أهلكت مالا لبدا ﴾ اللبد الكثير

BURHAN:v2p515/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p515/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p515/r2.claim: The pattern فعل can also be a verbal noun, as in هدى and تقى, or a form shifted from أفعل, as in أخر and أخرى.
BURHAN:v2p515/r2.anchor: ويكون مصدر كهدى وتقى ويكون معدولا عن أفعل من كذا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r7.claim: Al-aḥzāb is the plural of ḥizb; a ḥizb is a group distinguished from others by its own opinion.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r7.anchor: الأحزاب : جمع حزب . والحزب : الجماعة المنفردون برأيهم عن غيرهم

NASHR:v2p401/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p401/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p401/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the bāʾ in lubadan; the other readers pronounce it light.
NASHR:v2p401/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الباء، وقرأ الباقون بتخفيفها

ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r1.claim: The man boasts of spending abundant wealth on good works to gain praise rather than for God.
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r1.anchor: يقول على سبيل الفخر : { أهلكت مالاً لبداً } : أي في المكارم وما يحصل به الثناء

ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.claim: He should not think his deeds are hidden: watchers record what he does throughout life and preserve it until judgment.
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.anchor: بل عليه حفظة يكتبون ما يصدر منه من عمل في حياته ويحصونه إلى يوم الجزاء

ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r3.speaker: الجمهور وأبو جعفر وزيد بن علي ومجاهد وابن أبي الزناد
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r3.claim: The majority read lubadan with ḍamma on lām and fatḥa on bā; Abū Jaʿfar doubles bā, he and Zayd ibn ʿAlī also have a still bā, and Mujāhid and Ibn Abī al-Zinād use ḍamma on both.
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : لبداً ، بضم اللام وفتح الباء ؛ وأبو جعفر : بشدّ الباء ؛ وعنه وعن زيد بن علي : لبداً بسكون الباء

ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.claim: Another view identifies al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal, who sought the Prophet’s rulings on expiation and then boasted he had spent vast sums on expiations and liabilities.
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل ، وكان إذا أذنب استفتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فيأمره بالكفارة ، فقال : لقد أهلكت مالاً لبداً في الكفارات والتبعات

ALUSI:90:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:6/r1.claim: Lubadan means abundant, from something piled together; the speaker boasts in deluded pride over believers about wealth he spent ostentatiously, calling it destruction to show he expected no return.
ALUSI:90:6/r1.anchor: أي كثيراً من تلبد الشيء إذا اجتمع أي يقول ذلك وقت الاغترار فخراً ومباهاة

ALUSI:90:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:6/r2.claim: Another view says the wealth was spent in hostility toward the Messenger, with the complaint intended to injure him.
ALUSI:90:6/r2.anchor: وقيل يقول ذلك إظهاراً لشدة عداوته لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:90:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:6/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI:90:6/r3.claim: Muqātil says al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal sought the Prophet’s rulings on expiation after sins, then complained that obeying Muḥammad had cost him much in expiations and liabilities; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:90:6/r3.anchor: فعن مقاتل أن الحرث بن نوفل كان إذا أذنب استفتى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:90:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:6/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:6/r4.claim: A further view places the boast on the Day of Judgment, when the spending proves useless and so is described as wasted wealth.
ALUSI:90:6/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد ما تقدم أولاً إلا أن هذا القول وقت الانتقام منه وذلك يوم القيامة

ALUSI:90:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:6/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وزيد بن علي ومجاهد وابن أبي الزنا
ALUSI:90:6/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads lubbadan with a doubled b; Abū Jaʿfar and Zayd ibn ʿAlī also have lubdan with a still b, while Mujāhid and Ibn Abī al-Zinād read lubadan with ḍamma on both lām and bāʾ.
ALUSI:90:6/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر لبداً بشد الباء وعنه وعن زيد بن علي لبداً بسكون الباء وقرأ مجاهد وابن أبي الزنا لبداً بضم اللام والباء

BAGHAWI:90:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:6/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:90:6/r1.claim: Ahlaqt means spent; lubadan means abundant wealth piled up, spent in hostility toward Muhammad.
BAGHAWI:90:6/r1.anchor: يعني أنفقت ،   { مالاً لبداً } أي : كثيراً بعضه على بعض ،   من التلبيد ،   في عداوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI:90:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:6/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI:90:6/r2.claim: Abu Jafar reads lubad with a doubled bāʾ, treating it as the plural of labid, like rākʿ and rukkaʿ.
BAGHAWI:90:6/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر { لبد } بتشديد الباء على جمع لابد ،   مثل راكع وركع

BAGHAWI:90:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:6/r3.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI:90:6/r3.claim: The other readers use a light bāʾ, either as the plural of libda or as a singular form like Qutham and Hutam.
BAGHAWI:90:6/r3.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف على جمع لبدة ،   وقيل على الواحد مثل قثم وحطم

BAYDAWI:90:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:90:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:90:6/r1.claim: Lubad means a great amount, from the piling together of things.
BAYDAWI:90:6/r1.anchor: كثيرا من تلبد الشيء إذا اجتمع

BAYDAWI:90:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:90:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:90:6/r2.claim: He spent the wealth to be heard of and boast, or to oppose the Messenger.
BAYDAWI:90:6/r2.anchor: والمراد ما أنفقه سمعه ومفاخرة أو معاداة للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI:90:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:6/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:6/r6.claim: Only someone left with plenty after spending would boast of having squandered wealth; calling it “destroyed” belittles the amount and implies much more remains.
BIQAI:90:6/r6.anchor: لا يفتخر بالإنفاق إلا إذا أفضى إلى الإملاق

BIQAI:90:6/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:6/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:6/r7.claim: His boast reveals two further carnal desires: to claim pride and gratitude from all creation, and to possess wealth beyond imagining or containing.
BIQAI:90:6/r7.anchor: وهما إرادته أن يكون له الفخار والامتنان

BIQAI:90:6/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:6/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:6/r8.claim: The author cites prophetic sayings that a human would want another valley of gold and that nothing fills Adam's belly except dust, illustrating insatiable acquisitiveness.
BIQAI:90:6/r8.anchor: لا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب

BIQAI:90:6/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:6/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:6/r9.claim: Abu Jaʿfar's doubled consonant reading treats “lubad” as a plural like “rukkʿ” from “rākiʿ,” conveying an amount too numerous to count.
BIQAI:90:6/r9.anchor: بالتشديد على أنه جمع لا بد كركع وراكع

BIQAI:90:6/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:6/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:6/r10.claim: The speaker imagines his spending bought favors that bind free people to him, ensuring crowds answer his calls and obey him, so he thinks none can defy or diminish him.
BIQAI:90:6/r10.anchor: استعبدت به الأحرار في كل زمن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: Three-consonant nonverbs occur as both nouns and adjectives in several vocalic patterns; Sībawayh classifies them through paired examples.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: أما ما كان على ثلاثة أحرف من غير الأفعال فإنه يكون فعلا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: One pattern includes nouns عكم، جذع, and عذق alongside adjectives نقض، جلف، نضو، هرط, and صنع.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: ويكون فعلا في الأسماء والصفة فالأسماء نحو العكم والجذع والعذق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: Another pattern includes nouns البرد، القرط, and الحرض, while العبر، جد، المر, and الحلو are adjectives; عبر describes a camel for long journeys.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: والحرض وأما الصفات فنحو العبر يقال ناقة عبر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: Sībawayh gives جبل، جمل, and حمل as nouns and حدث، بطل، عزب, and وقل as adjectives for another shared pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: فالاسم نحو جبل وجمل وحمل والصفة نحو حدث وبطل وعزب ووقل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: A further shared pattern is illustrated by the nouns كتف، كبد, and فخذ and adjectives حذر، وجع, and حصر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: فالأسماء نحو كتف وكبد وفخذ والصفات نحو حذر ووجع وحصر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: Another form covers nouns رجل، سبع، عضد, and ضبع and adjectives حدث، حذر، خلط, and ندس.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: فالأسماء نحو رجل وسبع وعضد وضبع والصفة نحو حدث وحذر وخلط وندس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: Sībawayh classifies لبد as an adjective in a pattern also represented by صرد، نغر, and ربع, citing Qurʾan 90:6.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: Another pattern is used for nouns الضلع، العوض، الصغر, and العنب; عدى is the only adjective example he knows, a collective description rather than a broken plural from a singular.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: ولا نعلمه جاء صفة إلا في حرف من المعتل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.claim: إبل is the only rare noun he knows in a further pattern; another pattern occurs only in verbs, never nouns or adjectives.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمابنتالعربمنالأسماءوالصف.anchor: الاسم نحو إبل وهو قليل لا نعلم في الأسماء والصفات غيره

DURR:90:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:90:6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “libad” as abundant or plentiful.
DURR:90:6/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { مالاً لبداً } قال : كثيراً

DURR:90:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:6/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:90:6/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the speaker spent wealth to obstruct God's path.
DURR:90:6/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : { أهلكت مالاً لبداً } قال : أنفقت مالاً في الصد عن سبيل الله

IBNASHUR:90:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:6/r1.claim: The verse adds blameworthy speech to the human's inner faults: false boasting and self-praise for spending wealth wastefully rather than wisely.

IBNASHUR:90:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:6/r2.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs bragged about dissipating wealth and treated it as virtue because it suggested they did not care about their money.
IBNASHUR:90:6/r2.anchor: وقد كان أهل الجاهلية يتبجحون بإتلاف المال ويعدونه منقبة لإيذانه بقلة اكتراث صاحبه به

IBNASHUR:90:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:6/r3.speaker: عنترة
IBNASHUR:90:6/r3.claim: Antarah boasts of spending his wealth while keeping his honor intact, illustrating the pre-Islamic pride in lavish expenditure.

IBNASHUR:90:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:6/r4.claim: ‘He says’ is circumstantial with ‘the human’ in the preceding verse; this boasting is part of the hardship described there.
IBNASHUR:90:6/r4.anchor: { يقول أهلكت مالاً } في موضع الحال

IBNASHUR:90:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:7/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:90:7/r4.claim: The majority read lubadan with an ungeminated bāʾ, a plural of lubda for wool or hair matted and stuck together.
IBNASHUR:90:7/r4.anchor: بضم اللام وفتح الموحدة في قراءة الجمهور

IBNASHUR:90:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:7/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR:90:7/r5.claim: Abu Jafar reads lubbadan with a doubled bāʾ, either as a plural of lābid (‘gathered’) or a fuʿʿal noun like zummal and jubbaʾ.
IBNASHUR:90:7/r5.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر { لبَّداً } بضم اللام وتشديد الباء

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.claim: The disbeliever's boast that he squandered much wealth is a lie; God saw and recorded his deed, so there is no basis for his false claim.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.anchor: وكان قول هذا الكافر { أهلكت مالا لبدا } كذباً منه فلذلك قال تعالى

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r3.claim: The Prophet says that a servant's feet will not move on Judgment Day until asked about his lifetime, body, and wealth: where it was earned and spent.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لا تزول قدما عبد يوم القيامة حتى يسأل عن عمره فيما أفناه وجسمه فيما أبلاه وماله من أين كسبه وأين أنفقه )

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r4.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r4.claim: Most readers pronounce lubadan with ḍamma on the lām and fatḥa on the bāʾ.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r4.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله ( لبدا ) فقرأ جمهور القراء بضم اللام وفتح الباء

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r5.claim: Mujahid reads lubudan with ḍamma on both letters, as a plural of lubda or lubūd.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r5.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( لبدا ) بضمهما وذلك جمع لبدة أو جمع لبود بفتح اللام

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر يزيد
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far Yazid reads lubbadan with a doubled bāʾ, as a singular like raml or a collective of lābid; a sukūn-on-bāʾ form is also reported from him.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر يزيد : ( لبدا ) بضم اللام وفتح الباء وشدها فيكون مفردا نحو ( رمل )

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r7.claim: All these readings convey a great amount of wealth piled together through its density and abundance.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r7.anchor: والمعنى في هذه القراءات كلها مالا كثيرا متلبدا بعضه فوق بعض من التكاثف والكثرة

IBNKATHIR:90:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:6/r1.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والسدي وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR:90:6/r1.claim: They understand lubadan as a great deal: Adam's son boasts that he spent much money.

KASHSHAF:90:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:6/r1.claim: The spender boasts of the large wealth spent on what pre-Islamic people called generosity and styled as lofty deeds and objects of pride.
KASHSHAF:90:6/r1.anchor: يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها مكارم

KASHSHAF:90:7/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:7/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:7/r6.claim: Lubadan is read with ḍamma or kasra as a plural of lubda, a felted heap; other readings are lubudan, plural of lubūd, and lubbadan, plural of lābid.
KASHSHAF:90:7/r6.anchor: جمع لبدة ولبدة ،   وهو ما تلبد يريد الكثرة

MAWARDI:90:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r1.claim: Lubadan can mean plentiful; a cited line uses jamm in the sense of abundant forgiveness.
MAWARDI:90:6/r1.anchor: { يقول أهلكت مالاً لبداً } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : يعني كثيراً

MAWARDI:90:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r2.claim: It can mean wealth heaped together, as felt is called libd because its fibers gather and mat together.
MAWARDI:90:6/r2.anchor: الثاني : مجتمعاً بعضه على بعض ،   ومنه سمي اللبد لاجتماعه وتلبيد بعضه على بعض

MAWARDI:90:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r3.claim: It may mean old wealth, either deriving from eternity or emphasizing age by comparison to Labid, whom Arabs used as an exemplar of great age.
MAWARDI:90:6/r3.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : يعني مالاً قديماً ،   لاشتقاقه من الأبد ،   أو للمبالغة في قدمه

MAWARDI:90:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r4.claim: One reported identification is Abū al-Shadd al-Jumaḥī, who spent abundant wealth opposing the Messenger and blocking God's way.
MAWARDI:90:6/r4.anchor: وقيل إن هذا القائل أبو الشد الجمحي ،   أنفق مالا كثيراً في عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والصد عن سبيل الله

MAWARDI:90:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r5.claim: Another reported identification is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
MAWARDI:90:6/r5.anchor: وقيل بل هو{[3271]} النضر بن الحارث .

MAWARDI:90:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r6.claim: If the speaker is boasting about what he spent, that is an act of transgression.
MAWARDI:90:6/r6.anchor: أن يكون استطالة بما أنفق فيكون طغياناً منه

MAWARDI:90:6/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:6/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:6/r7.claim: Alternatively, he regrets the spending and laments its loss.
MAWARDI:90:6/r7.anchor: الثاني : أن يكون أسفاً عليه ،   فيكون ندماً منه .

NASAFI:90:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:6/r1.claim: Lubadan means abundant wealth, from lubda, a mass packed or gathered together.
NASAFI:90:6/r1.anchor: أي كثيراً جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد

NASAFI:90:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:6/r2.claim: He boasts of spending much on what pre-Islamic Arabs called generosity and noble deeds.
NASAFI:90:6/r2.anchor: يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها مكارم ومعالي

QURTUBI:90:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:6/r1.claim: أهلكت means I spent or expended.

QURTUBI:90:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:6/r2.claim: لبدا means a great amount of wealth gathered together.

QURTUBI:90:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:90:7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu al-Ashaddayn claimed to have spent much wealth in opposition to Muhammad but was lying.
QURTUBI:90:7/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال : كان أبو الأشدين يقول : أنفقت في عداوة محمد مالا كثيرا وهو في ذلك كاذب

QURTUBI:90:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r5.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI:90:7/r5.claim: Muqatil says it was revealed about al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal, who complained that expiations and expenses had consumed his wealth since he adopted Muhammad's religion.
QURTUBI:90:7/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في الحارث بن عامر بن نوفل ، أذنب فاستفتى النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ، فأمره أن يكفر . فقال : لقد ذهب مالي في الكفارات والنفقات

QURTUBI:90:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:7/r6.claim: Qurtubi says al-Harith's complaint could be boastful self-importance about his spending, and thus transgression, or regret over spending it.
QURTUBI:90:7/r6.anchor: وهذا القول منه يحتمل أن يكون استطالة بما أنفق ، فيكون طغيانا منه ، أو أسفا عليه ، فيكون ندما منه

QURTUBI:90:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
QURTUBI:90:7/r7.claim: Abu Jafar reads لبدا with doubled, open bāʾ, treating it as a plural like the plural forms of ركع, سجد, and شهد.
QURTUBI:90:7/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر  " مالا لبدا "  بتشديد الباء مفتوحة

QURTUBI:90:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r8.speaker: مجاهد وحميد
QURTUBI:90:7/r8.claim: Mujahid and Humayd read with ḍamma on both lām and bāʾ, lightly pronounced, as a plural of لبود.
QURTUBI:90:7/r8.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد بضم الباء واللام مخففا ، جمع لبود

QURTUBI:90:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r9.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI:90:7/r9.claim: The remaining readers lightly pronounce bāʾ with either ḍamma or kasra on lām; it is a plural of لبدة and means accumulated abundance.
QURTUBI:90:7/r9.anchor: الباقون بضم اللام وكسرها وفتح الباء مخففا ، جمع لبدة ولبدة

QURTUBI:90:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:7/r10.claim: Qurtubi notes that he discussed the reading and word in his commentary on Surat al-Jinn.
QURTUBI:90:7/r10.anchor: وقد مضى في سورة " الجن " القول فيه

RAZI:90:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:6/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI:90:6/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda derives lubad from piling things together and takes it to mean great wealth piled up.
RAZI:90:6/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : لبد ،   فعل من التلبيد

RAZI:90:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:6/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI:90:6/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this form indicates abundance, as in ḥaṭim for someone who breaks much.
RAZI:90:6/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : فعل للكثرة يقال رجل حطم

RAZI:90:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:6/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:90:6/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the singular is labda and lubad is its plural, though some treat lubad as singular; either way it denotes much.
RAZI:90:6/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : واحدته لبدة ولبد جمع

RAZI:90:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:6/r4.speaker: الليث
RAZI:90:6/r4.claim: Al-Layth glosses it as wealth so abundant that one does not fear its running out.
RAZI:90:6/r4.anchor: قال الليث : مال لبد لا يخاف فناؤه

RAZI:90:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:90:6/r5.claim: The disbeliever boasts that he spent greatly in hostility toward Muḥammad, on what pre-Islamic Arabs called generosity, nobility, and glory.
RAZI:90:6/r5.anchor: أن هذا الكافر يقول : أهلكت في عداوة محمد مالا كثيرا

RAZI:90:8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:90:8/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the boast asks who will hold the spender accountable; the answer is the One who created his organs.
RAZI:90:8/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن : قال { أهلكت مالا لبدا }
